leads.summary: Vertical bars read a different active format than the panel's new precision predicate
leads.consequence: On a left/right bar, BarWidget.qml chooses verticalFormat, whereas the panel always chooses format. Setting verticalFormat to HH:mm:ss with the default horizontal format leaves the panel on minute precision although the label ticks in seconds; setting format to HH:mm:ss while verticalFormat is HH\n—\nmm does the opposite and adds a per-second timer to an otherwise minute-only vertical bar. Neither situation changes the calendar's day rollover, but both contradict the stated lockstep guarantee. Settings injected after loading and edited live propagate via BarWidget.injectPanel; the key selection, not the storage scope, is at fault. No GUI runtime was run; the predicate and settings propagation are established from source.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1); corroboration; published

leads.summary: A hidden, date-only calendar clock runs its timer every second for a seconds-bearing horizontal format
leads.consequence: When the horizontal clock label shows seconds, the already loaded but closed calendar's separate SystemClock also switches from one tick a minute to one tick a second. Quickshell v0.3.1 schedules one independent QTimer per SystemClock and emits dateChanged on every tick. The panel's handler immediately returns on every tick except a change of day, so there is no seconds display to update and no user-visible improvement at rollover, only additional callbacks and wake opportunities even without the panel open (one per bar surface). The PR's statement that matching precision keeps the two halves in step is not a synchronization mechanism. If open #8653 also merges, its yearDone and yearDoneText bindings read this same clock.date and will be recalculated on every second tick instead of every minute (merged source at merges/8653-Panel.qml.merged:57-58,238). This is source-confirmed, not measured power use.
leads.triage: cost part already in Opus final (O1). #8653 part factual: verified by coordinator (refs/pr/8653 merged Panel.qml lines 57-58 bind yearDone/yearDoneText to clock.date; gh pr view 8653: OPEN). Published as one Details bullet.

leads.summary: New precision assertion passes even when panel seconds detection is disabled
leads.consequence: The test checks only the literal precision ternary in raw Panel.qml text; it never checks where panel showsSeconds comes from. A disposable copy with 'readonly property bool showsSeconds: false' passes the entire clock test at LC_ALL=C, including the new 'calendar panel ticks in lockstep' assertion. The new assertion does correctly fail at the merge-base, but cannot protect its stated seconds-format behaviour. panelSource also leaves comments unstripped, unlike widgetSource. Assert the panel predicate's connection to its effective format and strip comments from both source strings; cover verticalFormat when applicable.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** On a vertical bar the calendar panel reads `format`, not the bar's `verticalFormat`, so it can tick every second while the bar ticks once a minute.

### Panel precision ignores `verticalFormat` on vertical bars

`BarWidget.qml` derives `showsSeconds` from `verticalFormat` on a left or right bar, but the panel always reads `format`. With the stock `dddd HH:mm:ss` preset and the bar moved to a screen side, the bar stays on `SystemClock.Minutes` while the always-loaded panel ticks every second. **Impact:** nothing visible changes in normal running, but its handler runs every second and the new assertion also passes with `showsSeconds: false`.

**Suggested change:** Use `readonly property bool showsSeconds: hostWidget ? hostWidget.showsSeconds === true : false` (untested in QML), drop the panel's `configuredFormat`, and assert that derivation in `clock-test.sh`.

<details><summary>Reproducer: vertical bar (fails at 1d27029)</summary>

# Reproducer: panel precision does not follow the bar on a vertical bar

Reviewed head: `1d27029a9840618f66ee5e38ab73424804d43294`.

Scope: this evaluates the two `configuredFormat` binding expressions (from `BarWidget.qml` and `Panel.qml` as they are in the checkout) as plain JavaScript, with the bar orientation and the clock entry's settings supplied, then applies `Model.clockNeedsSeconds` as both files do. It does not run Quickshell or QML.

Scenario: the stock `dddd HH:mm:ss` preset is picked by right-clicking the clock on a horizontal bar (this writes `format`), then the bar is moved to a screen side. `shell.json` then holds `format: "dddd HH:mm:ss"` and the stock `verticalFormat: "HH\n—\nmm"`. The bar label shows `verticalFormat`; the panel reads `format`.

Save as `test/shell.d/clock-vertical-precision-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/clock-vertical-precision-test.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const fs = require('fs')
const calendar = requireFromRoot('shell/plugins/panels/clock/Model.js')

// Each file's configuredFormat binding, evaluated as plain JavaScript with the
// bar orientation and the clock entry's settings supplied.
function configuredFormat(file, vertical, settings) {
  const source = fs.readFileSync(root + '/shell/plugins/panels/clock/' + file, 'utf8')
  const match = source.match(/readonly property string configuredFormat:([\s\S]*?)\n  readonly property/)
  if (!match) fail(`${file} declares a configuredFormat binding`)
  const setting = (name, fallback) =>
    settings[name] === undefined || settings[name] === null ? fallback : settings[name]
  return Function('vertical', 'setting', `return (${match[1]})`)(vertical, setting)
}

// The stock "dddd HH:mm:ss" preset picked by right-clicking a horizontal bar,
// then the bar moved to a screen side: shell.json keeps both keys.
const settings = { format: 'dddd HH:mm:ss', verticalFormat: 'HH\n—\nmm' }

for (const vertical of [false, true]) {
  const bar = calendar.clockNeedsSeconds(configuredFormat('BarWidget.qml', vertical, settings))
  const panel = calendar.clockNeedsSeconds(configuredFormat('Panel.qml', vertical, settings))
  assertEqual(panel, bar, `calendar panel ticks per second exactly when the bar label does (${vertical ? 'vertical' : 'horizontal'} bar)`)
}
JS
```

Actual output at `1d27029a` (exit status 1):

```text
ok - calendar panel ticks per second exactly when the bar label does (horizontal bar)
expected: false
actual:   true
not ok - calendar panel ticks per second exactly when the bar label does (vertical bar)
```

The first line is the control: on a horizontal bar both files agree. On the vertical bar the bar label's format has no seconds (`expected: false`, the bar stays on `SystemClock.Minutes`) while the panel's flag is `true` (`SystemClock.Seconds`).

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: new assertion passes with a constant flag</summary>

# Reproducer: the new assertion passes when the panel's flag ignores the format

Reviewed head: `1d27029a9840618f66ee5e38ab73424804d43294`.

The new assertion (`test/shell.d/clock-test.sh`, "calendar panel ticks in lockstep with the bar clock") matches the text of the `precision:` line only. It does not check how the panel's `showsSeconds` is derived, so it still passes when the flag can never follow the format.

In a checkout of the PR head, make this one-line change to `shell/plugins/panels/clock/Panel.qml`:

```diff
--- a/shell/plugins/panels/clock/Panel.qml
+++ b/shell/plugins/panels/clock/Panel.qml
@@ -40,7 +40,7 @@
   // but ticking in lockstep with the bar avoids the two halves of the clock
   // disagreeing about precision.
   readonly property string configuredFormat: setting("format", "dddd HH:mm")
-  readonly property bool showsSeconds: Model.clockNeedsSeconds(configuredFormat)
+  readonly property bool showsSeconds: false
 
   // The month on screen. Stepping moves this and nothing else: the grid is
   // a read-out, not a picker, so there is no per-day cursor to keep in sync.
```

Then run `bash test/shell.d/clock-test.sh`. Actual output (relevant lines), exit status 0:

```text
ok - clock ticks per second only for a format that prints seconds
ok - calendar panel ticks in lockstep with the bar clock
ok - clock decides its tick rate from the format it is showing
```

For comparison, the head test file run against the merge-base `Panel.qml` (which still has `precision: SystemClock.Minutes`) stops at the new assertion, exit status 1:

```text
ok - clock ticks per second only for a format that prints seconds
not ok - calendar panel ticks in lockstep with the bar clock
```

Related, and shared with every other `panelSource` assertion in the file: `panelSource` is not comment-stripped (only `widgetSource` is). Replacing the `precision:` line with `precision: SystemClock.Minutes` and keeping the PR's line only as a `// precision: root.showsSeconds ? ...` comment also passes, exit status 0, with `ok - calendar panel ticks in lockstep with the bar clock`.

</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- On a horizontal bar the panel reads the same `format` key and `dddd HH:mm` default as the bar, so default users stay on minute precision.
- `clock-test.sh` passes at the head; the new assertion fails against the merge-base `Panel.qml`.
- The PR merges cleanly onto the current `quattro` tip and `clock-test.sh` passes there.

**What the panel's precision changes (from Quickshell `SystemClock` and Qt timer source, not measured):** the panel's clock only drives the midnight rollover, and both precisions fire at 00:00. The one difference is an already-open calendar catching up after a wall-clock jump (for example resume from suspend across midnight): about 1 s with `Seconds` versus up to about a minute with `Minutes`.

**Related open PRs:** #13751, #13613, #13546 and #13541 merge without text conflicts on top of this PR, and `clock-test.sh` passes on each merged copy. #13541 adds a refresh timer for minute formats that also refreshes the panel. #8653 binds the panel's year progress to `clock.date`, so with both merged that figure would recompute every second for seconds formats.
</details>
